practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 226 of the Constitution confers writ jurisdiction on High Courts not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Part III) but also for 'any other purpose' (such as statutory rights), making it wider in scope than Article 32.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article provides for the power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court within its jurisdiction?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 227 of the Constitution vests every High Court with the power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.q: Original jurisdiction of a High Court generally includes which of the following matters?
opts: Disputes relating to the election of Members of Parliament and State Legislatures
Disputes between the Centre and a State
Original criminal cases of all types arising anywhere in the country
practiceQuestions.sol: Original jurisdiction means the power of a High Court to hear disputes in the first instance, not by way of appeal. Election petitions regarding MPs and MLAs, revenue matters, and enforcement of fundamental rights fall under original jurisdiction. Centre-State disputes are exclusively under the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction (Article 131).

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional amendment Act curtailed the writ jurisdiction of High Courts introduced during the Emergency?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 drastically curtailed the writ jurisdiction of High Courts by removing the power to issue writs for 'any other purpose' and barring judicial review of central laws. (Note: Some changes were partly restored by the 43rd and 44th Amendments).

practiceQuestions.q: Can a High Court issue a writ to a person or authority outside its territorial jurisdiction?
opts: Yes, if the cause of action arises wholly or in part within its territorial jurisdiction.
Yes, automatically for any matter across India.
Only with the prior approval of the Supreme Court.

Following the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1963, Article 226 was amended to allow a High Court to issue writs to any person, government, or authority even outside its territorial jurisdiction, provided the cause of action arises wholly or in part within its territorial limits.

practiceQuestions.q: Which provision establishes every High Court as a Court of Record?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 215 of the Constitution states that every High Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 233, the appointment, posting, and promotion of district judges in a State are made by whom?
opts: The Governor of the State in consultation with the High Court
The Chief Justice of India directly
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 233 mandates that appointments of persons to be, and the posting and promotion of, district judges in any State shall be made by the Governor of the State in consultation with the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to such State.

practiceQuestions.q: The control over district courts and subordinate courts, including the posting and promotion of persons holding judicial office inferior to district judges, is vested in:
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 235 of the Constitution, the control over district courts and courts subordinate thereto—including posting, promotion, and grant of leave—is vested in the High Court.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Union Territories currently possesses its own High Court?
practiceQuestions.sol: Among Union Territories, Delhi and Jammu & Kashmir have their own High Courts. Puducherry falls under the Madras High Court, Andaman & Nicobar under Calcutta High Court, and Chandigarh under Punjab and Haryana High Court.

practiceQuestions.q: Parliament is empowered to extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or exclude it from, any Union Territory under which Article?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 230 of the Constitution grants Parliament the power to extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or exclude the jurisdiction of a High Court from, any Union Territory.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the writ jurisdiction of a High Court under Article 226 considered wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32?
opts: Because High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal/statutory rights.
Because the Supreme Court has no writ jurisdiction whatsoever.
Because High Court orders cannot be challenged in the Supreme Court.
Because High Courts can alter the Constitution while issuing writs.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 strictly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, Article 226 allows High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights as well as 'any other purpose', which includes ordinary legal and statutory rights.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 differ from the appellate jurisdiction of a High Court?
opts: Supervisory jurisdiction is administrative and judicial over all lower courts/tribunals suo motu, whereas appellate jurisdiction is invoked by an aggrieved party against specific judgments.
Supervisory jurisdiction can only be exercised over administrative officers, not courts.
Appellate jurisdiction applies only to High Court judges, while supervisory jurisdiction applies to Supreme Court judges.
There is no functional difference; both terms are legally synonymous.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 227 gives High Courts sweeping administrative and judicial superintendence over all subordinate courts and tribunals within their jurisdiction, even without a formal appeal. Appellate jurisdiction is triggered strictly through appeals filed by litigants against judgments or orders.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the legal implication of a High Court being designated as a 'Court of Record'?
opts: Its proceedings and judgments are preserved for perpetual memory and testimony, and its precedents are binding on subordinate courts.
It must record every single administrative file of the state government.
It can only handle criminal records and land registry records.
It is required to maintain records that cannot be reviewed by the Supreme Court.

A Court of Record means two things: (1) its judgments, proceedings, and acts are enrolled for perpetual memory and testimony, and (2) it has the power to punish for contempt of itself. Furthermore, its legal judgments serve as binding precedents for subordinate courts.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a High Court refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction under Article 226 on the ground of alternative remedy?
opts: Yes, existence of an alternative remedy is a rule of self-imposed restriction, though not an absolute bar.
No, Article 226 mandates that High Courts must hear every writ petition regardless of lower forums.
Yes, the Constitution strictly bars High Courts from entertaining any matter where a tribunal exists.
No, alternative remedies are only applicable to Supreme Court petitions.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court has held that the alternative remedy is a rule of discretion and self-imposed limitation rather than a bar to the jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226. In cases of violation of fundamental rights or natural justice, High Courts frequently entertain petitions despite alternative remedies.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power of judicial review exercised by High Courts derive its constitutional basis?
opts: Solely from Article 13 and Articles 226/227 read with the basic structure doctrine.
From an executive ordinance issued by the President of India.
From the Code of Civil Procedure passed by Parliament.
From international conventions signed by the Governor.

Judicial review in High Courts stems from constitutional provisions like Article 13 (laws inconsistent with fundamental rights are void), Article 226 (writ jurisdiction), and Article 227 (superintendence), reinforced by the Supreme Court ruling that judicial review is an unalterable part of the Basic Structure.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the structural relationship between a common High Court for two or more States and the respective State Governments?
opts: The High Court exercises independent jurisdiction over all participating states, and its expenses are allocated among the states as per presidential determination.
The High Court is subordinate to the executive branch of the state where its principal seat is located.
Each participating state appoints its own judges to the common High Court independently.
The Governor of the host state exercises administrative control over the entire common High Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 231, Parliament can establish a common High Court for two or more states. Judges are appointed by the President, and administrative expenses are allocated among the concerned states by the President based on financial capacities.

practiceQuestions.q: Why can a High Court's order under Article 226 be challenged in the Supreme Court?
opts: Because the Supreme Court exercises appellate jurisdiction over High Courts through Special Leave Petitions (Article 136) and regular appeals.
Because High Courts are merely administrative branches of the Supreme Court.
Because Article 226 explicitly mandates an automatic appeal to the Supreme Court for every writ.
Because state legislatures authorize such appeals.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court acts as the apex court with appellate jurisdiction over all High Courts in India. Orders passed under Article 226 can be appealed to the Supreme Court via Special Leave to Appeal under Article 136 or statutory appeals where applicable.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the scope of a High Court's revisional jurisdiction over subordinate courts?
opts: To correct jurisdictional errors, illegalities, or material irregularities in cases where no appeal lies to the High Court.
To rewrite the factual findings and evidence of all civil and criminal cases unconditionally.
To audit the financial accounts of district judges.
To review the administrative appointments made by the state cabinet.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code (CPC) or similar provisions, High Courts exercise revisional jurisdiction to examine if a subordinate court has exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise vested jurisdiction, or acted illegally in the exercise of its jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power of transfer under Article 228 operate with respect to subordinate courts?
opts: If the High Court is satisfied that a case pending in a subordinate court involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, it shall withdraw the case and resolve it or determine the constitutional question.
The High Court can transfer any criminal case to the Supreme Court without trial.
The Governor can transfer judges between High Courts through Article 228.
It allows litigants to transfer cases to international tribunals.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 228 empowers the High Court to withdraw a case pending in a subordinate court if it involves a substantial question of constitutional interpretation. The High Court can either dispose of the case itself or determine the constitutional question and return the case to the subordinate court.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are High Court decisions on tax matters or revenue tribunals subjected to restrictive appellate parameters?
opts: Because revenue statutes often provide specific appellate mechanisms, limiting High Court intervention primarily to substantial questions of law under reference/appeal provisions.
Because High Courts are constitutionally prohibited from touching financial matters.
Because tax disputes can only be settled through executive arbitration.
Because the Finance Minister acts as the final appellate judge.
practiceQuestions.sol: Statutory tax and revenue frameworks typically establish specialized appellate tribunals. High Courts intervene in these matters under their appellate or writ jurisdiction only when there is a jurisdictional error, a violation of principles of natural justice, or a substantial question of law.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the jurisdiction of High Courts:
1. The power of a High Court to issue writs under Article 226 is co-extensive with its territorial jurisdiction, and it cannot under any circumstances issue a writ to an authority located outside its state boundaries.
2. Unlike the Supreme Court, a High Court can refuse to exercise its writ jurisdiction if an adequate alternative remedy is available to the aggrieved party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because, per the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, a High Court can issue writs to authorities outside its territorial jurisdiction if the cause of action arises wholly or in part within its territorial limits. Statement 2 is correct; alternative remedy is a self-imposed restriction for High Courts under Article 226, unlike Article 32 where the right to move the Supreme Court itself is a Fundamental Right.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Court of Record status of High Courts:
1. Under Article 215, every High Court has the power to punish for contempt of itself, including criminal contempt.
2. The power of a High Court to punish for contempt is subject to state legislative control and can be curtailed by passing a state law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because while Article 215 makes High Courts a Court of Record with contempt powers, the power to punish for contempt of court is governed by the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, and is constitutionally rooted in Article 215, but 'criminal contempt' specifically relates to scandalizing the court, etc., yet neither state nor Parliament can override the constitutional contempt power inherent in a Court of Record. Statement 2 is incorrect because state legislatures cannot curtail the constitutional contempt powers of a High Court under Article 215.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227:
1. The power of superintendence conferred upon a High Court extends over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.
2. This supervisory power includes administrative superintendence as well as judicial superintendence, but it cannot be exercised suo motu without a formal application by a party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct as Article 227 clearly covers all courts and tribunals within the state/territorial jurisdiction. Statement 2 is incorrect because High Courts can exercise their supervisory jurisdiction suo motu (on their own motion) to correct gross failures of justice by subordinate courts or tribunals, without requiring a formal petition.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the control over subordinate judiciary (Articles 233-235):
1. The posting, promotion, and grant of leave to persons holding judicial office inferior to district judges are vested exclusively in the State Governor.
2. The consultation with the High Court by the Governor in the appointment of district judges is mandatory, and a disregard of High Court recommendations vitiates the appointment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because under Article 235, control over district courts and subordinate courts (including posting, promotion, and leave of judicial officers below district judges) is vested in the High Court, not the Governor. Statement 2 is correct; consultation with the High Court under Article 233 is mandatory, and appointments made without effective consultation are unconstitutional and void.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the original jurisdiction of High Courts:
1. The High Courts have original jurisdiction in matters relating to admiralty, probate, matrimonial, and contempt of court.
2. Election disputes regarding the election of members of the State Legislative Assembly fall within the original jurisdiction of the respective High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Original jurisdiction of certain High Courts (like Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras historically, or as conferred by statutes) includes admiralty, testamentary/probate, and matrimonial causes. Furthermore, under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, election petitions challenging the election of MPs and MLAs are filed directly in the respective High Court exercising original civil jurisdiction.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the power of Parliament to modify High Court jurisdictions:
1. Parliament can extend the jurisdiction of a High Court to, or exclude it from, any Union Territory by ordinary legislation.
2. The President of India by executive order can establish a common High Court for two or more states without requiring any parliamentary enactment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 230 empowers Parliament to extend or exclude High Court jurisdiction over Union Territories. Statement 2 is incorrect because establishing a common High Court for two or more states requires an enactment by Parliament under Article 231, not merely an executive order by the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the appellate jurisdiction of High Courts in criminal matters:
1. High Courts hear appeals from judgments of Sessions Judges and Additional Sessions Judges where the sentence of imprisonment exceeds seven years.
2. All death sentences passed by a Sessions Court require confirmation by the High Court before execution, regardless of whether the accused has filed an appeal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because under the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), appeals against convictions by Sessions Courts/Additional Sessions Courts lie to the High Court for *any* sentence of imprisonment (there is no 7-year threshold; appeals against smaller sentences from lower magistrates go to Sessions courts). Statement 2 is correct: under Section 366 of the CrPC, any death sentence passed by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by the High Court before it can be executed, operating independently of whether an appeal was filed.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of High Courts vis-à-vis the Supreme Court:
1. The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction over all judgments and orders of High Courts, making High Courts legally subordinate to the Supreme Court in the judicial hierarchy.
2. High Courts are bound to follow the law declared by the Supreme Court under Article 141, which is binding on all courts within the territory of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Supreme Court exercises appellate oversight over High Courts through Article 136 (SLP) and regular appeals, placing High Courts below it in the appellate hierarchy. Furthermore, Article 141 explicitly states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts (including High Courts) within India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 228 (Transfer of certain cases to High Court):
1. Article 228 can be invoked by a High Court only upon an application filed by the defendant in a subordinate court civil suit.
2. If the High Court determines the constitutional question involved in a withdrawn case, it must decide the entire case itself and cannot send it back to the subordinate court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Under Article 228, the High Court can withdraw a case suo motu or upon application, not restricted to a defendant's civil application. Furthermore, after determining the constitutional question, the High Court has the discretion either to dispose of the case itself or send it back to the subordinate court with a copy of its judgment to dispose of the case in conformity with the constitutional ruling.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative control and powers of High Courts:
1. The administrative control over the members of the state judicial service (below district judges) is vested in the High Court under Article 235.
2. A High Court has the power to transfer judges from one subordinate court to another within the state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 235 vests complete administrative control over district courts and subordinate courts, including postings, promotions, and transfers of judicial officers within the state, in the respective High Court.
